title: Derived tensor by a locally free line is the exact termwise equivalence
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme and $R$ a sheaf of commutative rings on its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], their unbounded derived category $D(R)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and the K-flat derived tensor [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent]. Let $P$ be a locally free rank-one $R$-module sheaf, meaning it is isomorphic to $R$ on a covering, and put $P^\vee=\mathcal Hom_R(P,R)$ [def-pur-sheaf-hom]. Use the ordinary sheaf tensor and its constraints [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product, lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed].

Both $P$ and $P^\vee$ are flat (their tensor functors are exact [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]), and $P[0]$ and $P^\vee[0]$ are K-flat [def-pc-kflat-complex]. The functors $F_P(K)=K\otimes_R^L P[0]$ and $F_{P^\vee}$ are naturally isomorphic to the functors induced by termwise ordinary tensor on arbitrary unbounded complexes. Evaluation and the symmetry give natural isomorphisms $F_{P^\vee}F_P\cong1$ and $F_PF_{P^\vee}\cong1$; they give inverse equivalences, are compatible with shifts and distinguished triangles [def-weil-triangulated-category], and identify $\mathcal H^i(F_PK)$ with $\mathcal H^i(K)\otimes_R P$ for every $i\in\mathbf Z$. The evaluation is the specified sheaf evaluation: on a local basis $p$ and its dual $p^\vee$, it is $(ap)\otimes(bp^\vee)\mapsto ab$, with inverse $a\mapsto(ap)\otimes p^\vee$. These maps satisfy the inverse-pair triangle identities. If $R$ is a sheaf of algebras over a commutative ring $B$, the functors and both evaluation isomorphisms are $B$-linear [def-weil-linear-functor]. No boundedness assumption on $K$ is imposed.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-flat-single-derived-normalization] to $L=P$ and $L=P^\vee$. Both singles are K-flat with flat terms, and $F_L\cong D(T_L)$ with the stated termwise comparison for every unbounded complex. The comparison commutes with all shifts and distinguished triangles, including their connecting maps. The same lemma supplies the natural derived cohomology isomorphisms required for $F_P$.

proof.text: Form the degreewise cancellation isomorphisms a_C and b_C from the ordinary evaluations and the mapHomologicalComplex identity comparison. Localize these isomorphisms with the pair comparison G(cP) followed by cD to define alpha and beta. Localization.liftNatTrans_app gives exactly the two required representative equations, and also alpha inverse on representatives. For the first triangle, apply Localization.natTrans_ext to the natural endomorphism F(alpha inverse) followed by beta_F. On Q(K), postcompose with cP(K), use naturality of beta and cP, cancel the inverse comparison components, and apply Q to the ordinary first triangle degreewise. This gives the identity on every derived object. The functors F,G, unit alpha inverse and counit beta therefore form an equivalence; its second triangle is Equivalence.unit_inverse_comp. The degreewise evaluations commute with every integer shift, including the degreewise identity comparison. The pair comparisons do as well. Whiskering alpha and beta by Q identifies them with the pasted comparisons, so shift compatibility descends by essential surjectivity of Q.

source.place: liftNatIso, liftNatTrans_app and natTrans_ext; direct naturality and cancellation prove the two localized triangle identities from the ordinary ones.

proof.text: If $R$ is a sheaf of $B$-algebras, Step 1 makes $T,S$ $B$-linear. By [lem-weil-linear-abelian-derived-category] and [lem-cbc-exact-linear-derived-functor], $Q,D(T),D(S)$ are $B$-linear. Conjugation by Step 2's isomorphisms preserves $F(bf)=bF(f)$ because composition is bilinear. The evaluations have $B$-linear components before localization by Step 1, and retain them under the linear $Q$ and the same comparisons. This proves every coefficient-linearity assertion without a bound on the complex.
